title: [Enhancement/A11y]: High-Contrast Focus Ring Customizer with Pulse Animation for Keyboard Navigation
body:
## Problem
Keyboard-only players and users with low visual acuity currently face difficulties tracking active element focus across dense game card grids and modal dialogs. Standard browser default focus outlines can blend into dark arcade backgrounds or get clipped by container overflow rules.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/a11y-focus-ring.css`:
   - Implement custom `:focus-visible` styling with dual-color concentric outlines (outer neon glow + inner crisp white contrast line) ensuring high contrast against any theme.
   - Add an optional gentle pulse animation for keyboard-focused elements that respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
2. Create modular controller `assets/js/a11y-focus-ring.js`:
   - Expose a focus style manager enabling users to select focus ring width (2px, 3px, 4px) and color preset (Neon Gold, Cyber Cyan, High-Vis White) in accessibility settings.
   - Persist user focus preferences in `localStorage` (`arcadeverse_focus_ring_pref`).
   - Listen for keyboard navigation (`Tab`, arrow keys) to activate focus indicators without impacting mouse clicks.
3. Zero external libraries, pure Vanilla JS/CSS3.
4. Add standalone test file `scripts/test-a11y-focus-ring.js` using Node.js built-in `node:test` or `assert` to verify settings persistence, DOM class application, and color mapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Keyboard navigation triggers clear, high-contrast focus rings on cards, buttons, and inputs.
- [ ] Focus ring width and color can be updated dynamically and persist across page reloads.
- [ ] Pulse animation smoothly disables when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active.
- [ ] Standalone test in `scripts/test-a11y-focus-ring.js` passes cleanly under `node`.
- [ ] Zero changes to protected files (`index.html`, `leaderboard.html`, `games-registry.js`).

title: [Enhancement/UX]: Game Card Favorite Collections Folder Organization System
body:
## Problem
Players can currently star individual favorite games, but cannot organize their starred games into custom playlists or folders (e.g. "Quick Break Games", "Multiplayer Favorites", "High Score Challenges"). As the game catalog expands to 100+ titles, a flat favorites list becomes unwieldy.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/favorite-folders.css`:
   - Styles for folder chips, playlist management drawer/modal, and folder badge tags on game cards.
2. Create modular manager `assets/js/favorite-folders.js`:
   - Implement `FavoriteFoldersManager` providing folder creation, renaming, deletion, and game assignment.
   - Store folder mapping in `localStorage` under `arcadeverse_favorite_folders`.
   - Provide methods: `createFolder(name)`, `deleteFolder(id)`, `addGameToFolder(folderId, gameId)`, `removeGameFromFolder(folderId, gameId)`, and `getFolders()`.
   - Add folder filter selector to the catalog header allowing players to view games belonging to a specific collection.
3. 100% Vanilla JS/CSS. Zero external frameworks or libraries.
4. Add automated test file `scripts/test-favorite-folders.js` validating folder CRUD operations and game tagging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users can create named collections and assign games to one or more folders.
- [ ] Catalog can be filtered by custom user-created folders.
- [ ] All folder structures and game assignments persist across sessions via `localStorage`.
- [ ] Automated test `scripts/test-favorite-folders.js` passes with 0 failures under `node`.
- [ ] No protected repository files modified.

title: [Enhancement/Catalog]: Quick Jump Alphabetical Index Bar for Fast Game Browsing
body:
## Problem
Browsing the extensive catalog requires extensive vertical scrolling. Players who know the exact name of the retro title they wish to play cannot jump directly to a specific alphabetical section (e.g. jumping straight to titles beginning with 'P' or 'S').

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/alphabetical-index.css`:
   - Sleek, sticky vertical alphabetical bar (A-Z, #) on desktop sidebars and horizontal scroller on mobile.
   - Visual active-letter highlight and disabled states for letters with 0 matching games.
2. Create modular script `assets/js/alphabetical-index.js`:
   - Dynamically inspect available games in catalog and compute existing letter anchors.
   - Smoothly scroll the viewport to the first game starting with the selected letter, accounting for sticky navbar height offset.
   - Update active letter indicator as the user scrolls past different alphabetical sections (IntersectionObserver or scroll listener).
3. Pure Vanilla JS/HTML5/CSS3 with zero external dependencies.
4. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-alphabetical-index.js` verifying letter grouping, anchor offset calculation, and empty state handling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Alphabetical index renders active letter indicators based on current catalog items.
- [ ] Clicking a letter jumps smoothly to the matching game card with appropriate header offset.
- [ ] Letters with no corresponding games display as inactive/disabled.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-alphabetical-index.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Clean modular architecture with zero modifications to protected files.

title: [Enhancement/UI]: Interactive Floating Back-To-Top Button with Circular Scroll Progress Ring
body:
## Problem
When users explore deep into the game catalog, returning to the navigation bar or search input requires long manual upward scrolling. A standard back-to-top button lacks visual feedback regarding total page progress.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/scroll-progress-top.css`:
   - Floating action button (FAB) positioned at bottom-right of the viewport.
   - SVG circular stroke indicator wrapping the arrow icon that fills dynamically from 0% to 100% based on scroll depth.
   - Neon glow transition on hover and smooth fade-in/fade-out when scrolling past 300px threshold.
2. Create modular controller `assets/js/scroll-progress-top.js`:
   - Calculate scroll percentage `(scrollTop / (scrollHeight - clientHeight)) * 100`.
   - Update SVG `stroke-dashoffset` in real-time using `requestAnimationFrame`.
   - Scroll smoothly to page top on click with keyboard accessibility (`Enter`, `Space`, `aria-label`).
3. Pure Vanilla JS/CSS3. Zero external libraries.
4. Add standalone test file `scripts/test-scroll-progress-top.js` verifying percentage calculation, threshold toggling, and aria accessibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Button smoothly appears when scrolled down and hides at top of page.
- [ ] SVG circle stroke accurately reflects scroll progress from 0% to 100%.
- [ ] Clicking the button smoothly scrolls to the top of the window.
- [ ] Fully accessible via keyboard and screen readers (`role="button"`, `aria-label`).
- [ ] Standalone test in `scripts/test-scroll-progress-top.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Enhancement/UX]: In-Browser Screenshot Capture & Instant Image Download Tool for Game Modals

2. Create modular script `assets/js/game-screenshot.js`:
   - Implement `GameScreenshotUtility` that targets the active game canvas or viewport container.
   - Convert canvas frame to PNG data URL via `canvas.toBlob()` / `canvas.toDataURL()`.
   - Watermark subtle retro "ArcadeVerse" logo stamp in bottom corner.
   - Trigger instant automatic file download (`ArcadeVerse-<Game>-<Timestamp>.png`) or copy image blob to system clipboard where supported.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas API. Zero npm packages (no html2canvas).
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-game-screenshot.js` verifying blob generation, timestamped filename format, and clipboard fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Captures game canvas and generates downloadable PNG file with branded timestamp filename.

title: [Enhancement/Catalog]: Multi-Tag Filtering System with AND-OR Logic Toggle
body:
## Problem
Catalog tag filters currently operate on a single-selection or implicit OR basis, preventing users from conducting refined multi-tag searches (e.g. finding games that are BOTH "multiplayer" AND "puzzle", or finding games that match ANY selected tag).

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/multi-tag-filter.css`:
   - Multi-select tag chips with active state highlights, tag remove crosses, and logic toggle switch ("Match ALL" vs "Match ANY").
2. Create modular controller `assets/js/multi-tag-filter.js`:
   - Support selecting multiple tags simultaneously.
   - Implement `filterGames(games, selectedTags, logicMode)`:
     - In AND mode (`all`): every game must contain all selected tags.
     - In OR mode (`any`): game must contain at least one of the selected tags.
   - Show dynamic result count badge updating in real-time.
3. Pure Vanilla JavaScript/CSS. Zero external frameworks.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-multi-tag-filter.js` testing AND/OR filtering logic against various game tag configurations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users can toggle multiple tags simultaneously.
- [ ] Interactive toggle switches between AND (all match) and OR (any match) filtering rules.
- [ ] Active tag count and filter summary are clearly visible.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-multi-tag-filter.js` passes 100% under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Enhancement/Audio]: Master Volume Keyboard Hotkeys HUD Overlay with Instant Visual Feedback
body:

   - Smooth fade-in and auto-fade-out after 1.5 seconds of inactivity.
2. Create modular controller `assets/js/volume-hotkeys.js`:
   - Listen for global keyboard shortcuts:
     - `[` or `Ctrl+Down`: Volume Down (-5%)
     - `]` or `Ctrl+Up`: Volume Up (+5%)
     - `M` (when not inside a text input): Toggle Mute
   - Update global Web Audio master gain node or audio element volume.
   - Display HUD overlay dynamically with current volume level and mute status.
   - Save volume level to `localStorage` (`arcadeverse_master_volume`).
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API. Zero dependencies.
4. Add standalone test file `scripts/test-volume-hotkeys.js` verifying shortcut event handling, boundary clamping (0% to 100%), and HUD trigger timing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts adjust volume and toggle mute smoothly.
- [ ] Visual HUD overlay appears on keypress and automatically fades out after brief pause.
- [ ] Volume settings persist across reloads.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-volume-hotkeys.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Clean isolation without editing protected files.

title: [Enhancement/A11y]: Screen Reader Live Region Announcer for Dynamic Catalog Filter Counts
body:
## Problem
When visually impaired players apply search queries or tag filters, the game grid updates visually, but assistive screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS) do not receive explicit feedback regarding the number of matching results or when no games match the query.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/a11y-live-announcer.css`:
   - Visually hidden yet accessible container class (`.sr-only` / `.visually-hidden`) for `aria-live` elements.
2. Create modular script `assets/js/a11y-live-announcer.js`:
   - Initialize persistent `div` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`.
   - Implement debounced announcer `announceCatalogUpdate(query, count, activeFilters)`:
     - Example: "Found 12 games matching 'Retro' in 'Action' category."
     - Example: "No games found matching 'XYZ'. Suggestions are available below."
   - Expose general announcement API `ArcadeAnnouncer.speak(message, priority)`.
3. 100% Vanilla JS. Zero dependencies.
4. Add automated test file `scripts/test-a11y-live-announcer.js` validating debouncing, message formatting, and DOM injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Search input and filter changes speak exact matching counts to screen readers via `aria-live`.
- [ ] Announcer does not cause visual layout shifts.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-a11y-live-announcer.js` passes with 0 errors under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Enhancement/UI]: Game Card Hover Sound Feedback with Subtle Retro Click Tones
body:
## Problem
Browsing game cards in classic arcade cabinet menus historically featured satisfying auditory blips and clicks on cursor movement. ArcadeVerse cards currently lack optional audio feedback on user interaction.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated controller `assets/js/card-hover-sound.js`:
   - Implement lightweight Web Audio API sound synthesizer producing a crisp, ultra-short (30ms) retro blip tone (sine/triangle wave at 880Hz decaying rapidly).
   - Attach debounced listener to game card `mouseenter` and keyboard `focus` events.
   - Respect global master mute and volume settings.
   - Provide "Card Hover SFX" toggle in audio settings (defaulting to enabled or disabled based on user preference).

title: [Feature/VFX]: Interactive 2D Water Surface Wave Ripple & Specular Refraction Canvas Sandbox
body:
## Problem
ArcadeVerse features static canvas backdrops, but lacks interactive fluid wave physics simulations where user cursor gestures and clicks generate realistic propagating wave interference patterns and specular light refraction.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/water-ripples.css`:
   - Fullscreen interactive canvas container and retro arcade control HUD with damping, tension, and rain drop frequency sliders.
2. Create modular physics engine `assets/js/water-ripples.js`:
   - Implement discrete 2D wave equation on dual grid buffers (previous and current heightfields).
   - Propagate wave energy each frame: `height[x, y] = (h[x-1,y] + h[x+1,y] + h[x,y-1] + h[x,y+1]) / 2 - prev_h[x, y]`, multiplied by damping factor.
   - Render surface with normal map calculation, simulated specular light reflection, and underwater caustic refraction.
   - Support cursor dragging (continuous wave generator), clicking (splash drop), and automated ambient rain drops mode.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/HTML5 Canvas API. Zero external math or physics engines.
4. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-water-ripples.js` verifying buffer swapping, damping decay, and heightfield clamping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 2D wave equation propagates smooth, realistic water ripples across canvas at 60 FPS.
- [ ] Clicking and dragging on canvas triggers dynamic wave splashes.
- [ ] Physics parameters (damping, tension, rain speed) can be tuned in real-time.

title: [Feature/Physics]: Interactive 2D Cloth & Soft-Body Mesh Verlet Integration Physics Engine

     - Drag Tool: Pull particles with dynamic spring tension.
     - Cut Tool: Sever spring constraints intersecting cursor trajectory to shred cloth.
